title: Clip-on lens for scanning tunneling luminescence microscopy
author: Cahlík, Müller, et al.

steps.title: Gather required components
steps.instruction: Collect all parts listed in the article: two aluminum pieces for the holder, 2 × M1.6 stainless‑steel mounting screws, Thorlabs lens 355397 (Ø7.2 mm, f = 11 mm, WD = 9.3 mm, NA = 0.3), Epotek E20H epoxy, Thorlabs VFA275A DN40CF viewport clamp, twelve 6 mm rods, cage adapter TTN247583, cage translator LCPX1/M, Z‑translation stage SM1ZA, aspheric coupling lens AC254‑030‑AB (Ø25.4 mm, f = 30 mm), XYZ translation stage CXYZ05A/M, fiber coupler SM05FC, multimode fiber M133L02 (Ø200 µm), MPD SPAD PD‑050‑CTE detector, Swabian Instruments Time Tagger Ultra, Fiberpoint 250MD alignment laser, and any cleaning/ sputtering equipment.

steps.title: Machine aluminum holder
steps.instruction: Machine the holder from two aluminum pieces so that it has a central groove to accept the flag‑style sample‑plate handle and a hole (≈5 mm grid paper size) for the lens; include two M1.6 mounting screw holes. The holder should position the lens 9 mm from the prospective sample centre (the intended focal point).

steps.title: Install aspheric lens
steps.instruction: Place the Thorlabs 355397 aspheric lens into the holder’s aperture, align its optical axis ≈30° from the sample‑transfer direction, and fix it with a few drops of UHV‑compatible epoxy (Epotek E20H). The lens focal point will be 2 mm above the sample plate (matching typical crystal thickness). Record that the lens opening angle is ≈34.7°, covering 0.285 sr (≈4.5 % of a hemisphere) and up to ≈9 % of the total solid angle for plasmonic emission.

steps.title: Transfer lens assembly
steps.instruction: Using the wobble stick, grasp the holder’s groove and attach it to the handle of a flag‑style sample plate. Move the assembly from the load‑lock through the manipulator and sample‑storage stages to the STM head and clip it onto the sample‑plate handle. Verify that the total assembly weight (lens, screws, holder) is 1.79 g.

steps.title: Set up ambient‑side optics
steps.instruction: Clamp a 30/60 mm Thorlabs cage system to the DN40CF viewport (VFA275A). Insert a translator stage (LCPX1/M) to correct the window‑axis offset. Mount the aspheric coupling lens (AC254‑030‑AB) on a Z‑translation stage (SM1ZA). Attach the fiber coupler (SM05FC) on an XYZ translation stage (CXYZ05A/M) and connect the multimode fiber (M133L02, Ø200 µm) to the single‑photon detector (MPD SPAD PD‑050‑CTE). Link the detector output to the Swabian Time Tagger Ultra for photon counting.

steps.title: Align optics (reverse path)
steps.instruction: Replace the detector with the Fiberpoint 250MD laser. Adjust the fiber‑to‑coupling‑lens distance on the Z‑stage until the fiber output sits at the focal point of the coupling lens (checked by a constant laser spot size on a white screen or on the sample). Use the XY and Z coarse stages to focus the laser spot onto the sample surface. Move the STM tip to the centre of the spot with the VTSTM coarse X/Y positioners, then auto‑approach to establish tunneling contact. This alignment defines the optical path for subsequent photon collection.

steps.title: Prepare sample and tip
steps.instruction: Mount an Au(111) or Ag(111) crystal on a sample plate. For Ag(111), sputter‑clean with 1.5 keV Ar⁺ ions for 45 min. Create Au‑ or Ag‑coated Pt/Ir tips by indenting the tip into the respective substrate. Keep the chamber at ~5 × 10⁻⁹ mbar and at room temperature (~300 K).

steps.title: Record photon count (steady state)
steps.instruction: Set the STM to a current setpoint of 45 nA and a bias of 3.6 V. Acquire photon counts with the detector; typical flux reaches up to 2 × 10⁵ cps. Note that the overall collection efficiency (including windows, fiber coupling and detector QEmax = 0.49 at 550 nm) lies between 0.7 % and 7 % (based on junction quantum efficiencies of 1 × 10⁻³–1 × 10⁻⁴).

steps.title: Sweep bias for plasmonic emission
steps.instruction: With the same tip‑sample contact, sweep the bias voltage from 1 V to 7 V while maintaining a constant current of 45 nA. Record photon counts versus bias; expect a ~500‑fold increase from 1 eV to a maximum around 4 eV for Ag(111).

steps.title: Map spatial luminescence
steps.instruction: Select a region containing different surface terminations (e.g., amorphous overlayer and Ag terraces). Set bias = 3.6 V, current = 5 nA, and a pixel dwell time of 500 ms. Use the STM controller’s pixel‑trigger to start/stop photon counting for each tip position, acquiring simultaneous topography and luminescence maps. Apply a linear line‑by‑line subtraction to the topography and a 1‑pixel Gaussian blur to the luminescence image if desired.

steps.title: Remove lens for deposition (optional)
steps.instruction: If material evaporation is required, detach the clip‑on lens from the sample plate, perform the deposition through the neighboring viewports, and re‑attach the lens using the wobble stick as described in step 4.

description: We have machined an ultra-high-vacuum compatible version of the clip-on lens from two pieces of aluminum (Fig. 1c). The weight of the entire assembly including screws and lens of 1.79 g does not affect the balance of our microscope, but the additional weight may need to be considered in other systems. Fig. 2 shows the STM head without and with a clip-on lens attached to the sample plate. To verify the optical path, we require at least one more optical element to collimate the parallelized light from the clip-on lens into our detector. Since the clip-on lens is the only optical element inside the vacuum chamber, we accordingly build the optical setup on the ambient side using commercially available off-the-shelf components, notably a 30/60 mm cage system clamped to the DN40CF viewport feedthrough (Thorlabs VFA275A) and also seen Fig. 2d. We correct for the parallel shift of the window's optical axis with respect to the lens’ optical axis using a translator stage (Thorlabs LCPX1/M). To couple the parallelized light into the detector, we use an aspheric lens (Thorlabs AC254–030-AB, Ø25.4 mm, f = 30 mm) that focuses the light into a multimode fiber (Thorlabs M133L02, Ø200 µm). The other side of the fiber is connected to a single photon detector (MPD SPAD PD-050-CTE) whose photon arrival clicks are registered with an event recorder (Swabian Instruments, Time Tagger Ultra).
